title: Local storage and privacy
description: Understand what Quickque stores locally, what leaves the device, and how licences and voice models are handled.
body:
# Local storage and privacy

Quickque is designed to keep scripts and voice work on the device. There is no Quickque cloud script library, cloud transcription service, analytics pipeline, or silent online fallback in the current app. Local-first is a boundary to understand, not a promise that every device or network is automatically safe.

## Plans and the temporary checkout

Quickque source and documentation remain available under the [MIT License](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/LICENSE). The packaged app is planned with Free, Monthly and Lifetime access. Free includes 30 seconds of Voice Follow per reader session. The Lifetime price is read from the `QUICKQUE_PRICE_GBP` environment variable and Monthly is always one tenth of that amount for each 30-day period; paid prices are not embedded in this guide.

Payments and paid activation are not implemented yet. The temporary dummy checkout collects no card, billing, contact or payment details, charges no money, and creates no order, licence, entitlement or download.

## What persists locally

1. The library envelope in local device storage includes live scripts, the active selection, Trash entries, custom order and sort mode.

2. Reader and appearance settings are stored separately from the library backup.

3. Successfully installed Flow and Chatterbox models are cached on the Mac and are not included in script backups. Chatterbox runtimes, models and related assets remain subject to their applicable Chatterbox, Resemble AI and third-party licence terms.

4. Generated rehearsal audio persists under the app's application-support storage until removed. Exported files remain user files after a subscription ends.

5. A paid licence stores its signed lease in macOS Keychain. Device identification uses a one-way hash of a stable Mac identifier; raw serial numbers, scripts, voices and microphone content are not sent to the licence service. A licence may be activated on no more than two devices.

## Microphone and local network

Local Flow captures the selected microphone only while listening. Audio and recognition events are processed in memory and are not saved as recordings or transcript logs.

Phone Remote exchanges minimal reader state and validated control commands over the local session. It does not serve script text, audio, transcripts, model files or library contents. Its local HTTP transport is unencrypted, so use it only on a trusted network.

## Updates

The packaged Mac app will use Sparkle 2. Sparkle contacts the Quickque HTTPS appcast and GitHub Releases to check for and download signed updates. It does not transmit scripts, voices or microphone data. Sparkle updates remain disabled until a signed appcast and production verification key are configured.

Lifetime includes future Quickque updates when released, but updates, support and future operating-system compatibility are not guaranteed. New paid features may require a separate licence or paid upgrade.

## Safer use

- Export a full backup before changing storage, deleting a script or uninstalling the app.
- Grant microphone permission only when intentionally starting Voice Follow.
- Pair Phone Remote only on a trusted local network and stop the session when finished.
- Share a specific meeting window rather than the whole display if the overlay should remain private.
- Never disable Gatekeeper for an unknown app or update.

Read [Requirements and installation](/guide/requirements-installation/) for the current release status and [Licence information](/license) for plan terms.
